title: The Mob at the Cotton Club and identifying with Black people
summary: The Cotton Club belonged to the mob and was segregated; Johnson could have passed but wanted to pull others along; he recalls Fats saying 'talk to me, baby'.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: J. C. was pretty reticent about talking about the Mob on tape. But one of the comments that he did make was that the Cotton Club belonged to the Mob and they had it pretty well segregated. He wrote shows for Texas Guynan and in the last two shows Texas Guynan, he mentioned, was ruled by the Mob.

I once asked him why he identified so strongly with the blacks at a time when things were so rough and he might have been able to pass. And he said, "I figured if I could make it, I could pull a few more along the way." On one of the tapes we have that Fats and J.
